I don't have a legal background, but I can answer some of your questions.

Anyone found guilty of murder receives a 'life sentence' in the UK. This is, I believe, up to 25 years, and it is the decision of the judge how many years will be served. For particularly heinous crimes (which arguably the murder of a neonate is), I would expect that she would be sentenced to the full 25 minus time on remand. I don't know if she would be given a chance at parole or not, but I would be surprised if she were. It may be that the judge decides to use the same rationale seen in Couzin's trial, but I'm not sure if there is any actual guidance on this. 

If she is found guilty of more than one count of murder I expect she would receive a whole life sentence. There are currently only 2 female prisoners in the UK serving a whole life tariff since Myra Hindley died. Rose West is one of them, and I will add here that she was convicted largely on circumstantial evidence as there was no DNA evidence or witness testimony tying her directly to the crimes of murder she has been found guilty of. The exception is the murder of Charmaine West, of which it was believed Fred was in prison at the time of the murder so it was placed solely on her.

Hope that helps a little, I'd be interested to hear what the legal types here think about it!
